ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Place a right triangular plate as shown in the figure, with point $C$ on the extension of $FD$, $AB\parallel CF$, $\angle F = \angle ACB = 90^\circ$, $\angle E = 30^\circ$, $\angle A = 45^\circ$, $AC = 6\sqrt{2}$. What is the length of $CD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the diagram, construct BM$\perp$FD at M,\\
In $\triangle ACB$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, $\angle A=45^\circ$, $AC=6\sqrt{2}$,\\
$\therefore BC=AC=6\sqrt{2}$,\\
$\because AB\parallel CF$,\\
$\therefore BM=BC\times\sin45^\circ=6\sqrt{2}\times \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}=6$,\\
$\therefore CM=BM=6$,\\
In $\triangle EFD$, $\angle F=90^\circ$, $\angle E=30^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle EDF=60^\circ$,\\
$\therefore MD=\frac{BM}{\tan60^\circ}=\frac{6}{\sqrt{3}}=2\sqrt{3}$,\\
$\therefore CD=CM-MD=6-2\sqrt{3}$.\\
Thus, the answer is: $CD=\boxed{6-2\sqrt{3}}$.

The hypotenuse ED goes from E down to the right to D, and point B lies on ED. Point A is on the upper right, AB is drawn as a horizontal line and is parallel to the bottom side CF; A, C, B form triangle ACB, C is on the bottom line, and the problem gives ∠ACB=90°. According to the method, draw BM⊥FD, with foot M. Reasoning: In △ACB, ∠ACB=90°, ∠A=45°, so △ACB is an isosceles right triangle, BC=AC=6√2. Because AB∥CF, the angle formed by BC and the horizontal bottom side is 45°, so in right triangle BCM, BM=BC·sin45°=6√2·√2/2=6, and CM=6. Also in △EFD, ∠F=90°, ∠E=30°, so ∠EDF=60°. Because B is on ED, and M, D are on the bottom line FD, in right triangle BMD there is ∠D=60°, thus MD=BM/tan60°=6/√3=2√3. In the figure, D is located between M and C, therefore CD=CM−MD=6−2√3.
